classes.name: Presidential elections
classes.finest_note: The commission publishes each candidate's votes by electoral area for 2015 (both rounds), 2020, and 2025 (both rounds, as images). It publishes nothing below the electoral area and no result for 1993 to 2011.
classes.note: The President is directly elected by secret ballot (Schedule 3 para 1) and must win more than half of the votes, with further ballots as the Electoral Commission directs (Schedule 3 para 5); a sole candidate is declared elected without a ballot (para 6). The term is five years, at most two terms since 2016 (art. 52). Since the Eleventh Amendment (in force 31 March 2025) the election is held on the Saturday in the fifth week before the term expires, on the same days as the Assembly's general election (Schedule 3 para 4, art. 79(1)). Polling runs over three days, the first two for the Inner Islands and other categories of voters. The one-party presidential elections of 1979 to 1989 are class president_1979.

classes.name: National Assembly general elections (directly elected members)
classes.finest_note: Each candidate's votes by electoral area for 2016, 2020, and 2025 (2025 as images); nothing below the electoral area and no result for 1993 to 2011.
classes.note: One member is directly elected by plurality in each electoral area (art. 78(a), 112(1)): 22 areas in 1993 (Schedule 7 para 10), 25 by 2016, and 26 since Ile Perseverance was added (S.I. 29 of 2016). A sole candidate is declared elected unopposed (art. 79(4)). Until 2025 a general election fell in the 57th to 59th month of a session or followed a dissolution; since the Eleventh Amendment it is held with the presidential election (art. 79(1) as substituted). The proportionally elected members are class assembly_pr, by-elections class assembly_by, and the one-party Assembly of 1979 to 1993 class assembly_1979.

classes.name: National Assembly proportionally elected members
classes.name_en: Proportionally elected members of the National Assembly
classes.finest_note: National only: the commission publishes each party's directly elected and nominated seats with its national vote.
classes.note: Up to ten members (art. 78(b)) allocated after each general election: since 21 February 1998 a party that polls 10% or more of the votes cast for its Assembly candidates nominates one member for each 10% (Schedule 4 para 2), the commission determines the entitlement and gazettes the names (paras 3-4). The first Assembly had eleven such members under the original scheme (Schedule 7 para 10(3)). No separate ballot is cast: the allocation is a declared outcome of the directly elected contests' party totals, so it adds seats but no votes.

classes.name: National Assembly by-elections
classes.note: When a directly elected member's seat falls vacant, a by-election is held within 30 days unless the vacancy falls within three months of the general-election window (art. 79(2), renumbered 79(9) in 2024); the Elections Act provides for the closing of the register before a by-election (s.9). A vacancy among the proportionally elected members is filled by the nominating party's notice to the Speaker, not by election (art. 81(4)). A tie for first place in an area is resolved by a second ballot there (Elections Act s.37(2)).

cadence.vacancy_rule: Within 30 days of the vacancy unless it falls within three months of the general-election window.

classes.disposition_reason: The commission's site and reports list no by-election and publish no by-election result; results are gazetted (Elections Act s.38(2)), but the Official Gazette's online archive (gazette.sc) starts in 2020.

classes.name: National referendums
classes.note: An Act provides for referendums (art. 164); Part IV of the Elections Act (s.54-) has the President refer an issue to the commission, which sets the date and the question. Alterations of Chapter I, Chapter III, art. 91, 110, or 111 need at least 60% in a referendum (art. 91(1)), and a referendum can also resolve a deadlock between the President and the Assembly (art. 110). The Constitution was prepared under the Constitution of Seychelles (Preparation and Promulgation) Act, 1992 (Schedule 7 para 1), outside the Elections Act; the commission's reports and site record no referendum since it came into force.

cadence.locator: https://ecs.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Ch.-262-Elections-Act.pdf (s.54: "Where any issue is required to be determined at a referendum, the President shall refer the issue to the Electoral Commission"; s.55: date by Gazette notice within seven days)

classes.disposition_reason: No referendum is recorded under the 1993 Constitution on the commission's site or in its reports; polls on the draft constitution under the 1992 Act were run by the Constitutional Commission, and no official host publishes their results online.

classes.name: Constitutional Commission election (1992)
classes.name_en: Election of the Constitutional Commission under the 1992 Act
classes.note: The 1993 Constitution was drafted by a Constitutional Commission under the Constitution of Seychelles (Preparation and Promulgation) Act, 1992; its chairman was the Director of Elections for the first elections of 1993 (Schedule 7 para 1, para 11). The class ended when the Constitution came into force on 21 June 1993.
classes.locator: https://ecs.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CAP42-Constituion.pdf (Schedule 7 para 1: "'Director of Elections' means the person holding office as Chairman of the Constitutional Commission immediately before the date of coming into force of this Constitution")
classes.disposition_reason: Abolished class with one election in 1992; no official host publishes its result online.

classes.name: People's Assembly elections under the one-party constitution (1979-1993)
classes.name_en: National Assembly elections of the one-party state
classes.note: Under the Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles Decree, 1979 (the "existing Constitution" the 1993 Constitution replaced, Schedule 7 para 1), the Assembly was elected from candidates of the sole lawful party. The class ended with the 1993 Constitution.
classes.locator: https://ecs.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CAP42-Constituion.pdf (Schedule 7 para 1: "'existing Constitution' means the Constitution contained in the Schedule to the Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles Decree, 1979")
classes.disposition_reason: Abolished class; no official host publishes results for the one-party Assembly elections online.

classes.name: Presidential elections under the one-party constitution (1979-1993)
classes.name_en: Presidential elections of the one-party state
classes.note: Under the 1979 Constitution the President was elected by the voters with a single candidate nominated by the sole lawful party. The class ended with the 1993 Constitution.
classes.locator: https://ecs.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CAP42-Constituion.pdf (Schedule 7 para 1, definition of the existing Constitution of 1979)
classes.disposition_reason: Abolished class; no official host publishes results for the single-candidate presidential elections online.

classes.name: Colonial legislature elections (to 1976)
classes.name_en: Legislative Council, Governing Council, and Legislative Assembly elections before independence
classes.note: Before independence on 29 June 1976 the colony elected members of its Legislative Council and later its Governing Council and Legislative Assembly. The class ended at independence.
classes.locator: https://ecs.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CAP42-Constituion.pdf (Schedule 2 para 1: "'Independence Day' means the 29th day of June, 1976")
classes.disposition_reason: Abolished class; the colonial returns are in the Seychelles Government Gazette and colonial reports, which no official host has online.

classes.name: Mayor of Victoria (proposed)
classes.note: In 2025 the commission planned a Mayor of Victoria election alongside the presidential and Assembly elections, as announced by the then President, but the government told it the law had not yet been passed, and no such Act appears in the Official Gazette's 2024 to 2026 lists. No other local office or council is elected in Seychelles under the Constitution or the Elections Act, which provide only for presidential, National Assembly, and referendum polls.
classes.locator: https://ecs.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/2025-First-Ballot-Election-Report.pdf (s.28: "the Electoral Commission was also planning to conduct the Mayoral election in concurrence with the Presidential and National Assembly elections ... informed that the law was yet to be passed for the Mayoral elections")
classes.disposition_reason: Not established: no law provides for the election, and none has been held. Reopen if an Act creating the office passes.

classes.name: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, and Leader of the Opposition
classes.name_en: Officers elected by the National Assembly
classes.note: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected by the Assembly (art. 83), and the Leader of the Opposition by the opposition members (art. 84).
classes.disposition_reason: Votes of members of the Assembly, not public elections.

classes.name: Vice-President
classes.note: Each presidential candidate designates a Vice-President on nomination (Schedule 3 para 2(1)(a)); the running mate is not voted on separately, and a mid-term vacancy is filled by the President with the Assembly's approval.
classes.disposition_reason: Elected on the President's ticket, with no separate ballot; held as the running mate of the presidential contest.

classes.name: Judges
classes.name_en: Judges of the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court
classes.note: The President appoints the Justices of Appeal and the Judges of the Supreme Court from candidates proposed by the Constitutional Appointments Authority (art. 123, 127).

classes.name: Party candidate selection
classes.note: Candidates file nominations with the commission on nomination day (Elections Act s.14-15); parties choose their candidates under their own rules, and the state runs no primaries.
classes.disposition_reason: Internal party processes, not run by the state.
